attacks.claim: The QA summary reports staff-pilot results (0 misdelivered texts, 2 copy fixes re-verified) as complete, but the pilot is scheduled for Nov 2-6 and today is 2026-10-26. The gate cannot rely on pilot evidence that does not yet exist.
attacks.evidence: | Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts; 2 copy fixes shipped and re-verified | ... 1. Nov 2-6: flags on for staff cards only (pilot above).

attacks.claim: The approved public announcement promises SMS alerts 'for every cardholder', but juvenile cards do not show the SMS option and cannot opt in directly. The announcement misstates who can receive the service.
attacks.evidence: Announcement text says exactly: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder." ... juvenile cards do not show it

attacks.claim: Patrons who chose SMS 'instead of' email may have email notices disabled. The rollback and cap fallback send them to their 'previous method', which may be disabled, so they could receive no hold notice when sms_holds is turned off or the spend cap is hit.
attacks.evidence: SMS: "in addition to (or instead of) the current email"; Rollback: "every opted-in patron gets hold notices by their previous method (email or automated phone call, kept on file)"

attacks.claim: The service runs in Spanish, but only the English opt-in disclosure, confirmation and message body are shown. The Spanish consent language, STOP/HELP wording and message text are not provided for review.
attacks.evidence: English and Spanish, following the patron's existing language preference. ... Message content: "Riverbend Library: 2 holds ready at Oak St locker..." (English only)

attacks.claim: The phone number that receives hold texts and locker codes can be added or changed from the account page with no stated re-authentication, step-up check or notice to the prior channel. A session takeover could redirect codes to an attacker's number.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: no re-authentication, MFA, or confirmation to the previous channel for changing the phone number. "My Account > Notifications > 'Text me when a hold is ready'. Phone field plus an unchecked checkbox"

attacks.claim: Confirmation texts are sent before any consent and there are no described rate limits per number, account or IP, nor country or premium-number restrictions. This enables SMS pumping, and because the $900 hard cap disables all SMS for every patron, the abuse becomes a service-wide availability failure.
attacks.evidence: "We send a confirmation text; texts start only after the patron replies YES." ... "On cap, texts stop and every opted-in patron falls back". ABSENT: rate limits on confirmation sends or number restrictions.

attacks.claim: Guardian-linked accounts can opt in to notifications about a juvenile's holds, but the artifact does not define which holds are sent, whether pickup codes are included, or whether the teen can see or object. This could expose a minor's hold activity and locker codes.
attacks.evidence: "guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account." ABSENT: scope of guardian notifications, whether pickup codes are included, and teen-level control for 13+ cards.

attacks.claim: The only automatic reroute to email or phone is the spend cap. If the SMS provider fails or degrades, nothing switches holds to the previous method. A delivery-failure alert only pages ops, so patrons may never learn a hold is ready.
attacks.evidence: "Alerts: delivery failures > 5% for 15 min" vs. "On cap, texts stop and every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method"

attacks.claim: STOP opt-outs depend on a signed webhook, but no retry, idempotency, dead-letter or event-lag monitoring is defined. If the endpoint is down or rejects events, opt-outs go unprocessed and patrons keep getting texts. The only webhook alert fires on signature failures, not on missed or delayed events.
attacks.evidence: "STOP ... is honored by the provider and our signed webhook, which clears the opt-in flag"; "webhook signature failures > 0"

attacks.claim: The rollout moves from a 64-staff pilot straight to all ~210k cardholders in one flag flip at 09:00, with no percentage ramp, branch-by-branch stage or volume checkpoint. A defect that appears only at scale would hit everyone at once, and the flag cannot recall texts already delivered.
attacks.evidence: "Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders; announcement goes out at 10:00 only after a smoke test of one live text and one locker pickup per branch."

attacks.claim: All quiet-hours messages queue to 08:00 and the full cardholder base is enabled at once. No throughput limit, send pacing or load test is described, and QA ran against the provider in test mode. A morning burst could trip provider rate limits, the spend cap or the 5% failure alert.
attacks.evidence: "anything later is queued to 08:00"; "against the production SMS provider account in test mode"

attacks.claim: At the $900 cap, every opted-in patron falls back to email or automated phone calls at the same moment. No capacity estimate for the phone or mail path is given, and the only alert is spend at 70%, not fallback volume. Ops could be overwhelmed exactly when texts stop.
attacks.evidence: "falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call, which stays on file), so no alert is lost"; "alert to ops at 70%"

attacks.claim: The dashboard shows queue depth and STOP rate, but no alert covers queue backlog, consent-write failures or fallback-path failures. A stuck queue could hold pickups past their deadlines without anyone being paged.
attacks.evidence: "Dashboard: texts sent, delivery rate, STOP rate, queue depth, locker cell status"; "Alerts: delivery failures > 5% for 15 min, webhook signature failures > 0, any locker bank offline > 10 min"

attacks.claim: Lockers run 24/7, but no overnight on-call is named. A bank may stay offline up to the 4 h vendor SLA while patrons are still directed to it, and no patron-facing fallback is defined for that window.
attacks.evidence: "pages branch manager + vendor; vendor SLA 4 h on-site"

attacks.claim: The locker_pickup rollback relies on manual staff moves of items to the holds shelf, with no time bound and no handling of codes already texted or items still in cells. Its only test is 1,200 staging rows, so production volume is unverified.
attacks.evidence: "staff move items to the holds shelf"; "tested in staging on 1,200 rows"

attacks.claim: The locker code is sent as plaintext SMS, so anyone who can read the phone (lock-screen preview, shared device, SIM swap) gets the second factor. Card-plus-code limits the exposure, but the trade-off is not discussed.
attacks.evidence: "Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14." and "The locker opens only after the patron scans their library card ... AND enters the code."

attacks.claim: Teen (13+) cardholders receive texts on their own phones, but the artifact has no documented analysis of minor-texting consent requirements.
attacks.evidence: "The option appears on adult and teen (13+) cards only"

attacks.claim: Accessibility is claimed for the opt-in form and locker touchscreen, but no WCAG conformance level or audit reference is cited for a public-entity deployment.
attacks.evidence: "screen has high-contrast mode, audio guidance through a headphone jack, and adjustable text size." ABSENT: WCAG level or audit reference.

attacks.claim: Phone numbers and consent records (timestamp, IP, checkbox text) have no defined retention period while the service is active or the flag is off, and TCPA consent-record retention is not addressed.
attacks.evidence: "Phone number and consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) are stored in the patron record"

attacks.claim: Lockout is per locker cell, so a card holder can make up to 5 guesses per cell across the 48 cells in a bank. The lockout can also be used to block a patron's own cell.
attacks.evidence: "5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff."

attacks.claim: The rollback runs a SQL script against production, but the artifact does not say who authorizes it or whether it has safeguards.
attacks.evidence: "remapped to the branch desk by `scripts/remap_locker_holds.sql` (tested in staging on 1,200 rows)"

attacks.claim: The sms_holds rollback does not say what happens to texts already queued when the flag is turned off.
attacks.evidence: "sms_holds off: no new texts; every opted-in patron gets hold notices by their previous method"

attacks.claim: The public announcement commits to permanent SMS and three-branch lockers, and the flag rollback does not retract it. The rollback plan does not address the resulting public commitment.
attacks.evidence: "Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder. 24/7 pickup lockers at Oak Street, Millbrook and Harbor."

attacks.claim: Permanent SMS withdrawal deletes numbers and consent records only in internal systems. It does not cover the provider's 30-day logs or carrier-side copies, and deletion cannot be verified.
attacks.evidence: "numbers and consent records are deleted within 30 days and patrons are emailed" / "it retains message logs 30 days"

attacks.claim: The SMS body reveals a named patron's hold count, location and pickup code. On a shared or lost phone this discloses borrowing activity, which the 'no titles' QA check does not test.
attacks.evidence: "Riverbend Library: 2 holds ready at Oak St locker. Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14."

attacks.claim: QA ran against the production provider account in test mode, so the '4 carriers Pass' result does not clearly establish live carrier delivery.
attacks.evidence: "against the production SMS provider account in test mode" alongside "Opt-in, YES confirm, STOP, HELP, re-opt-in (EN + ES) on 4 carriers | Pass"
